title: An Injectable and Drug-loaded Supramolecular Hydrogel for Local Catheter Injection into the Pig Heart
protocol: Dissolve 100 mg of the UPy-hydrogelator in a vial in 900 μl PBS pH 11.7 by stirring at 70 °C for 1 hr using a magnetic stirrer.
Cool the viscous solution down to room temperature.
Pipette the appropriate amount of drug or biomolecule dissolved in neutral PBS into the viscous solution and stir for 10 min to reach a uniform distribution.
Place the solution under an UV-lamp to sterilize for 1 hr.
Mount the 25 mm plate-plate geometry in the rheometer, set the temperature to 20 °C and load the plate with water to prevent evaporation of the gel during measurement.
Pipette 300 μl of the solution onto a 25 mm plate-plate geometry on a rheometer maintained at 20 °C.
Lower the plates to obtain a 0.5 mm gap distance.
Record shear viscosity as function of shear stress from 0.1 to 500 Pa with 10 points per decade.
Pipette 300 μl of the solution onto the plate.
Pipette a total of 4.2 μl of 1 M HCl at different places on the solution to induce gel formation.
Lower the plates to a gap distance of 0.5 mm.
Let the gel cure for approximately 30 minutes.
Measure storage and loss moduli at low frequency and strain, for example respectively 1 rad/sec and 0.5% during curing.
Record storage and loss moduli as a function of frequency (0.1-100 rad/sec) after curing.
Record storage and loss moduli as a function of strain (0.1-1,000%) after curing.
Transfer 100 µl of the viscous solution containing the drug or biomolecule into a poly(ethylene terephthalate) hanging cell culture insert for 24-wells plate with pore size 8.0 μm.
Cover the bottom of the inserts with Parafilm to prevent leakage while in liquid phase.
Pipette 1.4 µl of 1 M HCl on top of the viscous solution to reduce pH to approximately 7.0-7.2.
Let the gel cure inside the insert for about 30 minutes.
Remove the Parafilm from the inserts.
Place the insert in a 24-well plate and fill the well with 800 µl PBS pH 7.4.
Incubate the plate at 37 °C with slow rocking or shaking movement.
Fill remaining empty wells with PBS to prevent evaporation of the solvent.
Seal the 24-well plate with Parafilm.
Periodically refresh the PBS and analyze the removed PBS for released UPy erosion product or drug/biomolecule.
Quantify UPy erosion products by measuring UV absorbance at 265 nm.
Quantify pirfenidone by measuring UV absorbance at 320 nm.
Measure fluorescence emission of mRuby2 at 587 nm after excitation at 559 nm.
Translate measured absorption/emission values to concentrations via predetermined calibration curves.
Prepare calibration curves dissolving a series of known concentrations of the analyte in buffer and measure the UV absorbance or fluorescent emission of these samples.
Interpolate the data using a linear function to determine the concentration of the unknown samples.
For non-fluorescent proteins, use ELISA detection.
Fasting pigs for 12 hours, excluding water.
Sedate pigs by injecting midazolam 0.4 mg/kg, ketamine 10 mg/kg, and atropine 0.014 mg/kg intramuscularly.
Administer sodium thiopental 5 mg/kg intravenously to induce anesthesia.
Intubate the pig with an endotracheal tube.
Perform balloon-ventilation at a rate of 12/min if needed while transporting the animal to the operating theater.
Start mechanical positive pressure ventilation with FiO2 0.50, 10 ml/kg tidal volume, and a frequency of 12/min under continuous capnography upon arrival in the operation theater.
Apply vet ointment on the eyes to prevent dryness.
Start balanced anesthesia by continuous intravenous infusion of midazolam at 0.5 mg/kg/hr.
Infuse sufentanil continuously at 2.5 µg/kg/hr.
Infuse pancuronium bromide continuously at 0.1 mg/kg/hr.
Monitor ECG continuously during the procedure.
Monitor arterial blood pressure continuously during the procedure.
Maintain temperature monitoring throughout the anesthesia period.
Monitor capnography continuously during the procedure.
Intravenously infuse amiodarone at a rate of 4.3 mg/kg.
Place an intracardiac defibrillation catheter in the right ventricle using a venous sheath.
Occlude the left anterior descending artery distal to the second diagonal branch by intracoronary balloon for 90 minutes.
Anesthetize the pig following protocol steps 4.1.1-4.1.4.
Place an external reference patch on the pig’s back.
Secure vascular access via femoral artery according to protocol.
Obtain a biplane left ventricular angiogram in the 25° right anterior oblique view and 40° left anterior oblique view.
Estimate left ventricular size from the obtained angiogram.
Give heparin at a dose of 75 U/kg intravenously.
Advance an 8 French-mapping (D or F curve) catheter under fluoroscopic guidance to the descending aorta.
Position the catheter in the aortic arch and guide it across the aortic valve into the left ventricle.
Orientate the tip of the catheter towards the apex of the LV to acquire initial data points.
Sample outflow tract, lateral, and posterior points to form a 3D silhouette defining the ventricular borders.
Acquire subsequent endocardial segments by dragging the mapping catheter over the endocardium.
Define the target area where electrical activity is normal but mechanical movement is impaired (hibernating myocardium).
Replace the mapping catheter with an intramyocardial injection catheter composed of a 27-gauge needle and core lumen inside an 8 French catheter.
Load a volume-graded syringe with approximately 2 ml of hydrogel solution and attach it to a syringe pump.
Place 0.1 ml of the hydrogel solution into the needle dead space at both 0° and 90° flex positions.
Position the injection catheter tip across the aortic valve into the target area for intramyocardial injection.
Meet the following criteria for an injection position inside the target area:
Determine perpendicular position of the catheter to the LV wall.
Ensure excellent loop stability (<4 mm) as calculated by the EMM-system.
Underlying voltage should be >6.9 mV.
Advance the needle into the myocardium, confirmed by a premature ventricular contraction of the LV.
Inject 0.1-0.3 ml of hydrogel in a bolus at a constant rate of approximately 0.4-0.5 ml/min using the syringe pump.
Repeat injection at 6-10 different positions as diffuse as possible.
Post-procedure, humanely sacrifice the animal by exsanguination.
Cut the inferior caval vein and remove blood with a suction device.
Induce ventricular fibrillation by placing a 9 V battery on the apex.
